items.title: Negative-quantity entry errors (not returns)
items.clue_html: Some sales lines move stock in the wrong direction — yet they are not flagged as returns.
items.hint: Validity rules: quantity sign vs return flag.

items.title: Unit price 100x list (decimal shift)
items.clue_html: A few lines were rung up at a price wildly above the shelf price. A decimal point slipped.

items.title: Duplicate lines from re-ingestion
items.clue_html: The same line appears more than once. Someone loaded part of a file twice.

items.title: MCAR missingness
items.clue_html: Weather is sometimes missing — but does the gap depend on anything?

items.title: MAR missingness
items.clue_html: Age is missing far more often for one type of customer than another.
items.hint: Missingness rate by loyalty flag (customers table).

items.title: MNAR missingness
items.clue_html: Customers who did not report household size seem to shop differently from those who did.
items.ask: lines per basket ratio, missing ÷ known
items.hint: Compare baskets of customers with and without household_size.

items.title: Heavy-tailed spend: bulk buyers
items.clue_html: A small group of shoppers buys like a business, not a family.
items.ask: revenue share of the top 25 customers (0-1)
items.hint: Concentration: rank customers by revenue (clean errors first).

items.title: Store level shift
items.clue_html: One store's share of chain sales stepped down and never recovered.

items.title: Store-level promo experiment, true lift
items.clue_html: A store-level experiment hides a real effect — if you analyse at the right unit.
items.hint: weekly_store_category, store growth vs own baseline.

items.title: Cannibalisation
items.clue_html: When the big pack of a shampoo goes on promotion, its little sibling suffers.
items.ask: relative change in the small pack's category share (e.g. -0.10)

items.title: Seasonality and holidays
items.clue_html: Shoppers prefer certain days of the week.

items.title: Stockouts censor demand
items.clue_html: Empty shelves hide demand. How much demand never became sales? (instructor-verified — ask your facilitator)

items.title: Known price elasticity
items.clue_html: One category is far more price-sensitive than milk and yoghurt.
items.hint: price_elasticity_extract, log price with promo/display controls.

items.title: Simpson's paradox
items.clue_html: Promotions look bad for units per line overall — but good in every store format.
items.ask: overall relative difference, promo vs non-promo (e.g. -0.10)

items.title: Confounder: display paired with promo
items.clue_html: One in-store tactic almost never happens without another, so their effects cannot be separated.

items.title: Survivorship trap: delisted SKUs
items.clue_html: Snacks look like a growth story — if you only count the products still on the shelf.
items.ask: current-range Snacks growth, year 2 vs year 1 (fraction)

items.title: Returns-abuse cluster
items.clue_html: A cluster of customers in two stores returns a startling share of what they buy.
items.hint: Return rate per customer; who sits far from the rest?

items.title: Fabricated / rounded numbers
items.clue_html: One store's numbers are too round to be true.
items.hint: Benford by store vs peers; last-digit test.

items.title: Data drift point
items.clue_html: From one week onwards, discount depth for online orders changed scale.
items.ask: PSI of discount_pct, online promo lines, before vs after

items.title: Loyalty selection bias
items.clue_html: Loyalty members spend much more per basket. Is the programme responsible?
items.ask: naive member uplift in basket value (fraction)
items.hint: Compare baskets; then think about who joins.

items.title: Planted basket associations
items.clue_html: Two products are bought together far more often than chance.

items.title: Intermittent long tail
items.clue_html: Many SKUs sell nothing in most weeks.

items.title: Latent customer segments
items.clue_html: Shoppers fall into a handful of distinct types. How well does your clustering recover them? (instructor-verified)

items.title: A/B test with sample-ratio mismatch
items.clue_html: A 50/50 online test did not come out 50/50.

items.title: Impossible values
items.clue_html: Some customers are impossibly young or impossibly old.

items.title: Income missing not at random
items.clue_html: When income is missing, something else is different too.
items.ask: default rate ratio, missing ÷ known income

items.title: Rare events and base-rate trap
items.clue_html: Bad outcomes are rare — which makes some metrics useless.

items.title: Non-linear utilisation risk
items.clue_html: Risk is flat for a while, then climbs steeply with card usage.

items.title: Interaction: young x high DTI
items.clue_html: Being young is risky; so is high debt-to-income. Together they are worse than the sum.
items.hint: Logistic regression with an interaction (age<25 × DTI>0.45).

items.title: Multicollinearity
items.clue_html: Two predictors move together so tightly that their coefficients become unstable.
items.hint: VIF with income, limit, bureau score, DTI.

items.title: Fraud rings
items.clue_html: Some accounts share far more than a household would.
items.ask: number of linked groups with ≥ 6 accounts

items.title: Structuring below reporting threshold
items.clue_html: Cash deposits pile up just below a round number.

items.title: Benford violation
items.clue_html: One branch's transaction amounts do not follow nature's digits.

items.title: Leakage trap
items.clue_html: A model looks almost perfect — because it can see the future.

items.title: Population drift
items.clue_html: Recent applicants do not look like the ones the score was built on.

items.title: Concept drift
items.clue_html: The score ranks recent customers less well than older ones.
items.hint: AUC of app_score by vintage group.

items.title: Censoring for survival
items.clue_html: Most customers have not churned yet — and that matters for 'time to churn'.
items.hint: Survival: who has not had the event?

items.title: Heavy-tailed balances
items.clue_html: A tiny group holds an outsized share of balances.
items.ask: share of balances held by the top 1% (0-1)

items.title: Proxy for protected attribute
items.clue_html: Approval rates differ by a protected characteristic the model never sees.
items.ask: approval rate ratio B ÷ A (incl. declined applications)
items.hint: Approvals by group; which field is a proxy?

items.title: Champion/challenger effect
items.clue_html: A new collections strategy cures more accounts.

items.title: Insurance frequency-severity
items.clue_html: Claim counts vary more than a Poisson would allow.
items.ask: variance ÷ mean of claim counts per policy

items.title: Reject-inference trap
items.clue_html: The people we said no to are missing from every performance table.
